explanation: A dense dial that grows with context and with in-context repetition: in ordinary novel prose or code each non-initial token sits at 0.05-0.25 of max, so such text crosses 0.25 of max only once it runs past roughly 25-30 tokens (its noisiest token then reaches 0.25-0.4), while any recurring multi-token span or template (a re-run sentence, repeated '<|im_start|>'/'<|im_end|>' turns, parallel code lines or 'key: value,' rows, comma-separated lists, digit sequences) lifts the copy to 0.3-1.0 of max even in texts of 8-20 tokens. Predicted inactive (below 0.25 of max): texts under about 20 tokens with no repeated span, the first token, and texts of any length made of one repeated word or punctuation mark ('the the the', '. . .') or of bare space-separated word lists with no punctuation or function words ('Monday Tuesday Wednesday ...', 'one two three ...', 'dog house car tree ...'), which stay near 0.
